scenario: A recruiter creates one personal two-action Shortcut, assigns it to a supported iPhone Action Button, captures an authorized conversation screenshot in place, and later reviews, discards, or explicitly advances the local evidence without silent Agent processing.
frozen_evidence: artifact-r6.md with 14 matching SHA-256 source hashes

review_plan.reason: Evaluate first-time setup burden, interruption recovery, and whether the capture wedge helps a time-constrained independent recruiter.
Evaluate screenshot provenance, local privacy, state promotion, identity boundaries, rejection ordering, and reversibility.
Evaluate mobile hierarchy, touch targets, localization, Dynamic Type, status legibility, and recovery.
Evaluate candidate-data trust, purpose limitation, human agency, and avoidance of overclaiming.

findings.criterion: Setup burden ceiling versus real-world fallback
findings.observation: The exact two-action setup, empty-editor disclosure, and separated generic App Shortcuts are clear enough to approve, but first-time completion is proven in Simulator rather than through recruiter field use on physical Action Button phones.
findings.evidence: artifact-r6.md; AppSettingsView.swift; screenshots B16C3951-5CAB-4789-8354-231BFCCAF8EB.png and 60E55713-0E06-4074-AE5E-B03DD3C4AE66.png; r6 xcresult with 25 passing tests.
findings.user_impact: A busy recruiter gets an honest, short recipe, while real-world abandonment and detours remain unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current surface and measure fresh-install completion, detours, and time to first successful physical capture with first-time recruiters.
findings.verification: Run an uncoached physical-device study and record completion rate, detours, time to first success, and the recruiter's explanation of what Talent Signal verified.

findings.criterion: Fast continuation from receipt to review
findings.observation: Local receipt is now safely distinct from Assigned and the next app launch resumes pending review, but the receipt card itself does not directly open the oldest queued screenshot.
findings.user_impact: No false setup success is shown, though a recruiter visiting Settings can take an extra navigation step to reach the pending review.
findings.recommendation: When pending evidence exists, consider a direct Review pending screenshot action without changing assignment state.
findings.verification: Seed multiple pending items and prove the action opens the oldest item without duplication or assignment-state mutation.

strengths: All 14 r6 hashes matched and the final result bundle passed 25 tests.
The wedge stays narrow: one authorized conversation, exact evidence, unresolved and no-action outcomes, and explicit human review before downstream work.
missing_evidence: No connected physical iPhone proof of assignment and press.
No first-time recruiter field study of completion and abandonment.
No direct receipt-card jump to the oldest pending review item; safe next-launch recovery is proven instead.
open_questions: Do first-time recruiters interpret Local receipt as software-only evidence without opening the detail?
Does Other shortcuts aid discovery or cause setup detours on a physical device?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: r6 closes the receipt-ordering proof gap, while the broader post-save deletion and retraction inventory remains a separate lifecycle-governance follow-up.
findings.user_impact: The Action Button import itself is safe, but later retraction of already-reviewed downstream evidence still needs a system-wide proof.
findings.recommendation: Create a separate lifecycle artifact covering reviewed captures, identity cases, compiled wiki blocks, and derived canonical state.
findings.verification: Start after Save and check identity and prove which records are deleted, superseded, or intentionally retained with visible audit history.

strengths: All r6 hashes matched; the 25-test result includes corrupt, over-25-MiB, and over-80-megapixel rejection before both queueing and receipt.

The import validates first, stages second, and records a receipt only after successful local persistence; the local store has protection, backup exclusion, rollback, deduplication, FIFO, and per-item removal.

Will downstream lifecycle work preserve observed source, reviewer correction, derivation, and supersession as separate states?

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery
strengths: The frozen English and Chinese AX5 screens show one dominant task, an exact recipe, a truthful local boundary, a 44-point primary control, and no clipped or overlapping critical copy.
The assignment/receipt split and keep-or-discard recovery are visually clear and behaviorally covered by the r6 UI tests.

top_findings.reason: The app-owned flow is proven, but a real Action Button assignment and uncoached recruiter setup remain unmeasured.
top_findings.next_step: Run a physical-device first-use study without changing the approved setup surface first.
top_findings.verification: A fresh user assigns, captures, and correctly explains the receipt boundary without coaching.

top_findings.reason: The safe local import is complete, but system-wide retraction after explicit save is not part of this artifact.
top_findings.next_step: Create a separate downstream data inventory and deletion/supersession test.
top_findings.verification: The follow-up proves an authorized delete or supersession outcome for every derived record.

top_findings.reason: Automatic next-launch recovery is proven, while the Settings receipt itself remains informational.
top_findings.next_step: Evaluate a direct oldest-pending-review action only if field observation shows this detour matters.
top_findings.verification: The optional action opens exactly one oldest item without mutating assignment state.

agreements: The exact Take Screenshot → Review screenshot recipe is the lightest truthful setup because iOS keeps Action Button assignment user-owned.
The button press creates protected local pending evidence and performs no hidden network or Agent work.
Assigned and Local receipt are separate truths, and neither claims proof of a physical press.
Human review, identity uncertainty, keep, discard, retry, and no-action remain available before downstream promotion.
r6 resolves the prior medium safety evidence gap with one executable rejection-ordering test.

veto_resolution.veto: A screenshot receipt promoted the user's manual Action Button assignment state in the first review round.
veto_resolution.evidence: r6 writes only the receipt timestamp and CandidateSignalUITests/testActionButtonAssignmentAndReceiptStatesRemainIndependent() passes across all four states and relaunch.

adjudication.rationale: All four selected specialist packets validate against the frozen r6 artifact; scores are 3, 3, 4, and 4 without averaging, and no current veto, blocker, high, or medium finding remains. The app-owned capture path, privacy boundary, state truth, recovery, localization, and human authorization gate are directly evidenced. Physical hardware, field comprehension, live VoiceOver, and broader post-save lifecycle governance remain explicitly isolated follow-up evidence rather than false release claims.
